Note: the bundle's digest field states 26.3% YoY revenue growth for DXCM, which conflicts with the source earnings release's own stated 13%/12% organic figure -- I am citing the sourced, lower number as the reliable one and flagging the discrepancy rather than using the more flattering figure. The balance sheet is net cash (-0.81x net debt/EBITDA, $1.95B cash, minimal debt), TTM free cash flow more than doubled to $1.405B, and the company is returning capital (3.88% TTM buyback yield, diluted shares down 4.4% YoY). Ownership_flow shows institutional accumulation aligned with the rising price, and sell-side has been raising targets all week (BTIG to $90, Stifel to $95, Truist to $93, WebSearch-verified, not bundle-sourced) following the print. The stock pulled back 4.92% in its most recent session after tagging a 52-week high three sessions earlier -- I could not confirm a specific negative catalyst for that single-session drop through today's degraded news feed, so I am treating it as digestion after a strong run (RSI 61.5, not overbought; still above both the 50- and 200-day averages) rather than a broken thesis, and sizing/stopping so that I am proven wrong cheaply if it is more than that.
catalysts: Q2 FY2026 earnings beat + raised FY26 revenue guidance to $5.18-5.25B (~11-13% growth), reported 2026-07-30

Stelo OTC CGM relaunch (new AI-driven insights app, expanded Type 2 non-insulin access) widening the addressable market beyond core insulin users
